text: @slothtron/dsh-fff 是面向 DSH Web 的工作区文件搜索插件。它注册 fffind 模糊路径搜索与 glob 查询，以及 ffgrep 文本搜索工具，并由常驻索引辅助进程处理查询。工具按当前会话工作区切换索引，可查找文件路径、按字面/正则/模糊方式查找文件内容，并返回行号和上下文。Web 设置页还可切换文件变更实时监听。适合需要在 DSH 会话中快速定位项目文件或代码内容的用户；安装依赖 @ff-labs/fff-node，无需额外 API 密钥。

@slothtron/dsh-fff adds file search to DSH Web. fffind searches session workspace paths by fuzzy query or glob; ffgrep searches file contents in plain, regex, or fuzzy mode and returns matching lines. A Web settings card toggles live watching. It needs @ff-labs/fff-node and no API key.
想按模糊文件名快速找到当前项目里的代码文件
帮我在这个 DSH 会话的工作区里搜某段代码文本
能不能用 glob 模式列出符合路径规则的文件？
@slothtron/dsh-fff 的功能「路径搜索」：通过 fffind 按模糊路径查询当前会话工作区，也可将查询作为 glob 模式；结果包含匹配路径及数量。
@slothtron/dsh-fff 的功能「内容搜索」：通过 ffgrep 在当前工作区按字面、正则或模糊方式搜索文本，可设置结果数量和前后文，并返回文件、行号及匹配内容。

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · @slothtron/dsh-fff：FFF (Fast File Finder) tools for DeepSeek Harness. Registers `fffind` (fuzzy file-path search / glob) and `ffgrep` (content grep) as model tools, backed by a resident [`@ff-labs/fff-node`](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff) index whose root **follows the current session workspace**.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add ./dsh-fff
@slothtron/dsh-fff README · or from git:：dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:Slothtron/dsh-fff

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · restart dsh web for the bundle layer to activate：```

This links the bundle into the profile's `node_modules`, appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles`, and inserts the `fff-tools` plugin row. Remove with `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove @slothtron/dsh-fff`.
section: restart dsh web for the bundle layer to activate

text: @slothtron/dsh-fff README · restart dsh web for the bundle layer to activate：The bundle declares `@ff-labs/fff-node` as a dependency, so pnpm installs the platform native binary (`@ff-labs/fff-bin-<platform>`) alongside. Everything else — `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` for the settings schema, and the browser-half externals — resolves from the DSH installation's `profiles/node_modules` fallback at runtime, so the plugin ships with **zero additional npm dependencies** beyond the native fff SDK.
section: restart dsh web for the bundle layer to activate

text:
@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Build (browser half)：The Host half is plain ESM JavaScript (`lib/*.js`), no build step. The browser half (`src/client/*`) is bundled once with esbuild and committed as `lib/client.js`:

```sh
node scripts/build.mjs   # esbuild is resolved from the DSH checkout ($DSH_SOURCE or ~/.dsh/source/current)
```

`lib/client.js` is a build artifact committed to git, so a git install needs no `prepare` script or build allowlisting.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · How it works：The native fff SDK cannot load inside the harness process, so the plugin spawns a **resident helper** (`lib/fff-server.mjs`) that owns one `FileFinder` hot index and answers line-delimited JSON on stdio — the same spawn-a-native-binary pattern as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search`.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · How it works：Each tool call resolves the calling session's workspace from `exec.agent.session.header.cwd`. When it differs from the helper's current index root, the plugin asks the helper to `reindex` (and waits for the new scan, ~50–100 ms) before querying. This is what the MCP-injected `fff-mcp` could not do: its index root was fixed by the process cwd's git-root probe, so it searched the wrong tree for every session in another workspace.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose | Parameters |
|------|---------|------------|
| `fffind` | Fuzzy file-path search (or glob) | `query` (req), `pageSize`, `useGlob` |
| `ffgrep` | Content grep (plain/regex/fuzzy) | `query` (req), `mode`, `pageSize`, `beforeContext`, `afterContext`, `classifyDefinitions` |

Both return `{ base, totalMatched, totalFiles, items }`; `output.render` presents the matches as model text.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `basePath` | `''` | Fixed index root; empty resolves from the session workspace per call |
| `scanTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Wait budget for an index scan / reindex |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `30000` | RPC timeout per tool call |
| `serverPath` | packaged copy | Absolute path to the helper script |
| `enableWatch` | `false` | Static fallback for the background file watcher; the web settings card flips it live at runtime |

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Watch toggle (runtime settings)：The bundle ships a browser half (the `dsh.client` entry) that registers a card
in the web **Settings → Plugins** tab. The card's switch flips the helper's
background file watcher without a restart: the Host half exposes the `dsh-fff`
settings namespace, and a change calls `reconfigure`, which destroys the
resident index and rebuilds it with the new watch mode on the next search.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Watch toggle (runtime settings)：- **On** — the index reflects filesystem changes (create/edit/delete) live.
- **Off** (default) — snapshot semantics: the index updates only when the
  session workspace switches (a reindex), not on in-workspace edits.

A deployment without a settings provider (or with the browser half absent)
keeps the `enableWatch` composition value, so the switch is additive and never
required.
@slothtron/dsh-fff README · What the model sees：Two tool schemas (`fffind`, `ffgrep`) with descriptions that direct fuzzy/indexed search over the built-in ripgrep tools.
@slothtron/dsh-fff README · Token effect：Fixed: two tool definitions are always registered while the plugin is loaded; their descriptions are part of the assembled tool catalog.
@slothtron/dsh-fff README · KV Cache effect：The tool-catalog prefix is stable while the plugin is loaded; no per-request dynamic content is injected into the prompt.

@slothtron/dsh-fff README · UI presentation (search cards)：`presentationMeta` is a pure, byte-bounded projection (capped at 32 KB) persisted with the session log, so the card reproduces on replay without persisting the canonical value; malformed or absent metadata falls back to the generic card. The model-facing text (`output.render`) is unchanged.
